Milestone Evaluation:

I had the 5k race on Saturday. I hadn't run much outside during training and when I did, it was on flat terrain. The race had a hill to climb early with a sharper incline on the way down. I was afraid that the hill would really take the wind out of me but I made it without walking. In fact, I made it to about 1.5 miles before walking for about 50 yards. At 2 miles, I walked for another stretch before running the rest of the race. The biggest problem I had was the fact that I was constantly trying to pass people and would have to slow down if I couldn't find a way around them at that second. I started further away from the start line than I should have, which left me with people constantly in the way. I never got close the speed that I normally do on the treadmill. I feel like I could have knocked some of my time off if I was able to go at my pace.

Overall, I am pleased with my performance. I barely walked during the whole race. The time sucked but I did have a hill and way more people than I thought ahead of me to block the way. I may try for another 5k sometime in mid to late summer.

I did not make my goal of being able to do 5k in 30 minutes by the race. I am a little disappointed but I cam fairly close to it before. I don't know when I'll make this goal since I am now going to be focusing on weightlifting for my exercises. I want to be able to easily do pull-ups at Half Mudder since I will need to be able to throw my own weight around. I will still do some cardio, but it will be more sporadic and dependent on my friend's schedule.

The Half Mudder is now 6 weeks away. My goals for it are to be able to run 5 miles in an hour without feeling terrible, and to be able to perform 5 reps of pull-ups and dips. As my body fat goes down, these should become easier. I'm happy with my progress on the assisted pull-up/dips machine but it had slowed down. By my birthday in late April, I should be able to do 5 pull-up & dips without any assistance and complete that goal.
